releases.title: web first: six examples to try in Claude or ChatGPT, played step by step, with questions under each; no hooks on the front pages; an account page of our own; R002 read point by point
releases.notes: R002, the lead's second memo, kept verbatim and read in 26 points with screenshots of v0.2.2. The home page and start here are now in the browser: open Claude or ChatGPT, ask, paste one line, ask again, new chat with the line first. Six examples in tabs, simplest first (hello world, stay on topic, no web search, keep a secret, drafts never send, refunds up to 50 pounds), each versioned, each in a chat frame drawn like Claude's or ChatGPT's, each with the prompts to copy and five questions whose answers the reader emails. Every demo on the site can be played, paused, stepped back and forward. No hook and nothing to install on the front pages; the Claude Code behaviour policies are kept further down /policies/ under a warning. The account strip sits under the hero; the account page is our own view of the meter, without the newsroom's personas; the meter's reader card under each page is gone, and it still charges. Cards show pictures of where they go. The register has 37 proposals; D1 is recorded as declined at v0.2.2 and reversed at v0.2.3, with why. Questions Q4 to Q6 for the lead.

releases.title: the feedback loop: the lead's first review read point by point with screenshots, five invented users run through v0.2.1, and one register of 23 proposals each with a decision and a reason
releases.notes: R001, Dinis Cruz's first impression, kept verbatim with our reading point by point and screenshots of v0.2.1: the hook answers a question nobody has asked yet. Study S1: five invented users (Sam, Nadia, Marcus, Joan, Tomas) drove v0.2.1 one screenshot at a time; 29 findings, each checked (24 confirmed, 4 partly, 1 artefact). /feedback/: one line by email, a voice memo your Claude turns into a review, or a Claude interview. The register: 23 proposals; 8 done in this release (the feedback pages, the study, what the 50 pounds is, no more 'start a new session', did it work and the hook fails open, each hook in plain words with how to turn it off, line-only pages, start here's status line moved to its foot); the guided path (P1, P2) proposed and held for the lead's further memos; 5 declined with reasons; questions Q1 to Q3 for the lead.

releases.title: the customer first: £50 of credit metered by SG Meter, six behaviour policies with tested hooks, storyboards and demos
releases.notes: The home page is now the customer's: £50.00 of credit, one worry, one line, one hook, one prompt to try it, with the programme's logistics moved to the programme pages. Every page has a price by its kind (1p the home page, 2p a page, 10p a storyboard, 50p a behaviour policy, £1.00 the starter pack), charged by how far it is read by SG Meter v1.4.1 from api.newsroom.sgit.ai release v0.2.5, pinned and loaded with its manifest's hash; nothing is blocked and there is no payment link yet, so top-ups are simulated and say so. Six behaviour policies from riskmandate.ai's rules: four for Claude Code with a line and a PreToolUse hook (secrets, pushes, deletes, its own permissions), each hook tested with an allowed twin for every refusal; two for ChatGPT and Claude with a line, said to be an expectation only; and a starter pack Claude Code installs from one prompt, showing every file first. Three storyboards drawn by the kit from api.storyboards.sgit.ai v0.1.0, loaded with integrity, its delay attributes allowed by hash and nothing else inline; three demos of a session on a drawn laptop or browser, labelled as illustrations. The header fits every width from 320 to 1440 pixels with the balance in it. From this release every push moves the third number.

releases.title: six themes, the newsroom's five mapped onto RiskMandate's look plus its own dark; the header fits an iPad
releases.notes: A theme pill in the header picks one of six, kept in this browser: RiskMandate (the default, riskmandate.ai's paper and green), Canvas (its dark, from the dark hero band), and newsroom.sgit.ai's Night, Ember, Paper and Blueprint, mapped onto this site's tokens. Every colour now lives in assets/themes.css and nowhere else; site.css reads tokens only. A new test fails the build on a theme missing a token, a colour written outside that file, or a pair under its contrast in any theme; it found riskmandate.ai's green at 4.24:1 on its own alternate band, so the link accent is one shade darker. The header lost the first-batch stage pill, gained the picker beside the version, and now folds its links behind the menu button below 1100px: between 1040 and 1200 the version chip used to run past the right edge and the page scrolled sideways, which is an iPad in landscape. Wide tables scroll inside themselves on a phone instead of widening the customers page. docs/ops/themes.md says how it works and how to add a seventh.

releases.title: the repository moved to Risk-Mandate; the source links and the DNS target follow it
releases.notes: The lead moved the repository from the SGit-AI organisation to Risk-Mandate/Risk-Mandate-AI__Website__Customers between the first push and the first CI run, and pointed customers.riskmandate.ai at risk-mandate.github.io. Every source link on the site, the release script's Actions lookup, the participant disclosure and the DNS line in needs.md now name the new home; the corrections file records the move as C9. Nothing else changed.

releases.title: the first customers site: the brief, the start-here page, the batch, the steps and the gate
releases.notes: The site exists, as customers.riskmandate.ai, a sub-site of riskmandate.ai, built from the newsroom brief of 20 October 2026 and the voice memo that followed it the same day. What is here: the brief published in full with its corrections file beside it; a start-here page in order; the programme pages (customers not beta users, credit and the meter, the seven milestone steps, the daily follow-up, what we want to discover, the next batch); a page per customer generated from data/customers.json with no contact details in it; the reality file; the team as files; the review folder with the brief as intent; and the eight-check gate with a leak tripwire and the house words. What is not here: the meter (the newsroom's, not yet wired to this site), a form, any customer's private details, and the derived half of the review folder. Every number on a page is counted from a file.
